extracted.intended_audience: public water system operators, state drinking water program regulators, and approved laboratories
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements for source water monitoring, analytical methods, reporting, grandfathering, disinfection profiling/benchmarking, bin classification, and Cryptosporidium/E. coli/turbidity treatment for public water systems under EPA Part 141 subparts H and related sections. Covers sampling schedules/locations, approved methods and labs, data reporting elements, treatment obligations by bin/mean levels, and compliance timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source water monitoring start/round timing (§141.701)
rubrics_metrics.description: The system must begin a second round of source water monitoring no later than 6 years following initial bin classification under § 141.710 or determination of the mean Cryptosporidium level under § 141.712, as applicable. The requirements of § 141.701(f) apply to subpart H systems that begin operation after the monitoring start date applicable to the system's size under paragraph (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing ties monitoring rounds to initial bin classification or mean determination. Systems beginning operation after monitoring start dates are subject to § 141.701(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring violation for failure to collect required samples
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to collect any source water sample required under this section in accordance with the sampling schedule, sampling location, analytical method, approved laboratory, and reporting requirements of §§ 141.702 through 141.706 is a monitoring violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncompliance can be triggered by errors in schedule adherence, sampling location, method, lab approval, or reporting. Systems must follow all referenced sections to avoid violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling schedule submission (§141.702(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems required to conduct source water monitoring under § 141.701 must submit a sampling schedule that specifies the calendar dates when the system will collect each required sample. Systems must submit sampling schedules no later than 3 months prior to the applicable date listed in § 141.701(c) for each round of required monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems serving ≥10,000 must submit initial-round schedules to EPA electronically at https://intranet.epa.gov/lt2/ (or an EPA-approved alternative if unable). Systems serving <10,000 submit schedules to the State. Schedules for second round are submitted to the State. If EPA/State does not respond, systems sample at reported schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling date window and exceptions (§141.702(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must collect samples within two days before or two days after the dates indicated in their sampling schedule (i.e., within a five-day period around the schedule date) unless specific exceptions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: (1) Extreme danger or unavoidable situation — sample as close as feasible and submit explanation to State with shipment; (2) Loss of valid result due to equipment failure, sample damage, method QC failure, or lab failure — must collect replacement sample within 21 days of learning result cannot be reported, unless infeasible or State approves alternate date; submit explanation with shipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescheduling after missed samples (§141.702(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems that fail to meet the criteria of paragraph (b) for any source water sample required under § 141.701 must revise their sampling schedules to add dates for collecting all missed samples and submit the revised schedule to the State for approval prior to collecting missed samples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A proactive revised schedule and prior State approval are required before collecting missed samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling locations per plant and combined-intake handling (§141.703(a), (e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must collect samples for each plant that treats a surface water or GWUDI source. Where multiple plants draw from the same influent (same pipe/intake), the State may approve one set of monitoring results to satisfy § 141.701 for all plants. For multiple sources, if a sampling tap exists where sources are combined prior to treatment, sample from that tap; otherwise collect at each source near the intake on the same day and composite or calculate weighted averages per § 141.703(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Composite option: combine volumes weighted by source proportion at collection time. Separate analysis option: analyze each source and calculate weighted average by flow fraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling before chemical treatment and bank filtration rules (§141.703(b)-(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must collect source water samples prior to chemical treatment unless the State approves collection after treatment because pre-treatment sampling is not feasible and treatment is unlikely to affect analysis. Systems that recycle filter backwash must collect prior to point of backwash addition. Bank filtration: systems receiving Cryptosporidium treatment credit for bank filtration must collect samples in surface water prior to bank filtration; systems using bank filtration as pretreatment to a filtration plant must collect from the well (after bank filtration) and cannot receive treatment credit for bank filtration during monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State approval required to sample post-treatment; use must be consistent with routine practice. Sampling after bank filtration disqualifies bank filtration treatment credit under § 141.717(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of sampling location description (§141.703(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must submit a description of their sampling location(s) to the State at the same time as the sampling schedule. This description must address the position of the sampling location in relation to the system's water source(s) and treatment processes, including pretreatment, points of chemical treatment, and filter backwash recycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the State does not respond regarding locations, the system must sample at the reported locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cryptosporidium analytical methods and sample volume (§141.704(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must analyze for Cryptosporidium using Method 1623 (2005) or Method 1622 (2005), which are incorporated by reference, or alternative methods listed in appendix A to subpart C. Systems must analyze at least a 10 L sample or a packed pellet volume of at least 2 mL as generated by the methods; systems unable to process 10 L must analyze as much as can be filtered by two EPA-approved filters up to 2 mL packed pellet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matrix spike (MS) samples must be spiked and filtered by an EPA-approved Cryptosporidium lab. If MS volume >10 L, field can filter all but 10 L and ship remainder for lab spiking. Flow cytometer-counted spiking suspensions must be used for MS and OPR samples. Methods incorporated by reference — copies and inspection locations provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: E. coli analytical methods, holding time, and storage (§141.704(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must use methods for enumeration of E. coli in source water approved in § 136.3(a) or alternative methods listed in appendix A. Time from sample collection to initiation of analysis may not exceed 30 hours unless State approves up to 48 hours (samples held 30–48 hours must be analyzed by Colilert version of Standard Method 9223B). Systems must maintain samples between 0 °C and 10 °C during storage and transit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State may grant case-by-case extension to 48 hours if 30-hour analysis is not feasible. Use specified method when holding times extended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turbidity measurement methods (§141.704(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must use methods for turbidity measurement approved in § 141.74(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to § 141.74(a)(1) for approved turbidity measurement techniques and instrumentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved laboratories for Cryptosporidium, E. coli, and turbidity (§141.705)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cryptosporidium samples must be analyzed by a laboratory approved under EPA's Laboratory Quality Assurance Evaluation Program for Analysis of Cryptosporidium in Water or a lab certified by an equivalent State program. Any lab certified by EPA, NELAC, or the State for total coliform or fecal coliform analysis under § 141.74 is approved for E. coli analysis when using the same technique. Turbidity measurements must be made by a party approved by the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laboratory approval/certification status is mandatory for validity of monitoring results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting deadlines and recipients (§141.706(a)-(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must report results from source water monitoring required under § 141.701 no later than 10 days after the end of the first month following the month when the sample is collected. Systems serving at least 10,000 people must report initial round results to EPA electronically (or approved alternative). Systems serving fewer than 10,000 must report initial round results to the State. All systems must report second-round results to the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic reporting required for large systems unless alternative approved. Timely reporting is required to meet monitoring obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cryptosporidium reporting data elements (§141.706(e)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must report for each Cryptosporidium analysis: PWS ID; Facility ID; Sample collection date; Sample type (field or matrix spike); Sample volume filtered (L), to nearest 1/4 L; Was 100% of filtered volume examined; Number of oocysts counted. Additional reporting for matrix spike samples: sample volume spiked and estimated number of oocysts spiked (not required for field samples). For <10 L filtered or <100% examined, report number of filters used and packed pellet volume. For <100% examined, report volume of resuspended concentrate and volume processed through immunomagnetic separation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete data elements and additional fields for partial-volume or MS samples are required to support data validity and calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: E. coli reporting data elements (§141.706(e)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must report for each E. coli analysis: PWS ID; Facility ID; Sample collection date; Analytical method number; Method type; Source type (flowing stream, lake/reservoir, GWUDI); E. coli /100 mL; Turbidity. Systems serving <10,000 not required to report turbidity with their E. coli results if not required to monitor turbidity under § 141.701.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report method identifiers and source type to allow interpretation and comparability of results; turbidity reporting conditional on monitoring requirements and system size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grandfathering previously collected data (§141.707 overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems may comply with initial source water monitoring by grandfathering sample results collected before monitoring was required if sample results and analysis meet the section's criteria and the State approves. A filtered system may grandfather Cryptosporidium samples without corresponding E. coli and turbidity samples (and then is not required to collect E. coli and turbidity when completing Cryptosporidium monitoring under § 141.701(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grandfathered data must meet analytical, lab, location, frequency, representativeness, and documentation criteria listed in the section; State approval is required. Filtered systems have limited flexibility regarding E. coli/turbidity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical and volume criteria for grandfathered Cryptosporidium samples (§141.707(c)(1)-(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Laboratories must have analyzed Cryptosporidium samples using one of the listed analytical methods (Methods 1622/1623 across specified years) and must have analyzed at least 10 L of sample or at least 2 mL of packed pellet or as much as could be filtered by two EPA-approved filters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grandfathered analyses must use approved/incorporated methods and meet the minimum volume/filter criteria identical to current monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling frequency and representativeness for grandfathered data (§141.707(e)-(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Cryptosporidium samples were required to be collected no less frequently than each calendar month on a regular schedule, beginning no earlier than January 1999. The State may approve grandfathering where there are time gaps if the system conducts additional monitoring to ensure data are seasonally representative and unbiased. If sampling frequency varied within months, systems must follow monthly averaging procedures when calculating bin classification or mean concentration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State may require additional monitoring to fill gaps or ensure representativeness; systems must report intent and results by specified deadlines and provide documentation/certifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grandfathering reporting and certification requirements (§141.707(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems requesting to grandfather must report intent (number of results, first/last sample dates, whether additional monitoring will be conducted) by the sampling-schedule deadline, and must report previously collected monitoring results with documentation within two months after applicable date in § 141.701(c). For each sample, systems must report applicable data elements in § 141.706; must certify that reported results include all results during the period and that samples were representative and source waters have not changed; must provide lab certification that QC criteria in methods were met or provide bench sheets and sample examination report forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed documentation and formal certifications (system and laboratory) support grandfathering approval; deadlines differ by system size for recipient (EPA vs State).

rubrics_metrics.name: State review/disapproval and replacement monitoring for grandfathered data (§141.707(g)-(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the State determines the previously collected data were generated during abnormal source water conditions (e.g., drought), the State may disapprove the data or approve them only if additional monitoring is reported to ensure representativeness. If previously collected data that fully meet required sample counts have some data rejected for noncompliance, systems must conduct additional monitoring to replace rejected data on a State-approved schedule; systems need not begin additional monitoring until two months after notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State has discretion to ensure data reflect average conditions; rejected data trigger replacement monitoring with an administrative delay before start.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and requirements when making significant disinfection change (§141.708)
rubrics_metrics.description: After initial source water monitoring, a system planning a significant change to its disinfection practice must develop disinfection profiles and calculate disinfection benchmarks for Giardia lamblia and viruses as described in § 141.709. Prior to changing practice, the system must notify the State and include a completed disinfection profile and benchmark, a description of the proposed change, and an analysis of how the change will affect the current level of disinfection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant changes are defined (point of disinfection, disinfectant identity, disinfection process, or other State-identified significant modifications). Notification must be accompanied by technical profiles and impact analysis before change implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disinfection profiling monitoring frequency and method requirements (§141.709(a)-(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems required to develop disinfection profiles must monitor at least weekly for 12 consecutive months to determine total log inactivation for Giardia lamblia and viruses. If monitoring more frequently, spacing must be even. Systems operating fewer than 12 months per year must monitor weekly during operation. Determine Giardia inactivation based on CT99.9 values in § 141.74(b) tables; determine virus inactivation using a State-approved protocol. Systems with single or multiple disinfectant points have specific monitoring parameter requirements (temperature, pH for chlorine, contact time, residual concentrations) during peak hourly flow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems may use up to three years of existing equivalent data if no significant changes have occurred, or use prior profiles from other sections if applicable. Monitoring parameters required differ by disinfectant and must be measured during peak hourly flow or State-approved alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disinfection inactivation calculation and benchmark procedure (§141.709(d)-(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must calculate total inactivation ratio for Giardia lamblia via CTcalc/CT99.9 methods: single-segment or successive-segment approaches depending on disinfectant points; total logs = (CTcalc/CT99.9) × 3.0. Virus inactivation calculated by State-approved protocol. For benchmarks, determine lowest mean monthly level of Giardia and virus inactivation for each year; the disinfection benchmark is the lowest monthly mean (one year) or the mean of lowest monthly means (multiple years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For multi-segment systems sum sequential CTcalc/CT99.9 values. Benchmarks are conservative (lowest monthly means) to represent minimum typical inactivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bin classification calculation for filtered systems (§141.710)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filtered systems must calculate an initial Cryptosporidium bin concentration per plant after initial monitoring using reported results and procedures: (1) ≥48 samples — bin concentration = arithmetic mean of all sample concentrations; (2) 24–47 samples — bin concentration = highest arithmetic mean of all concentrations in any 12 consecutive months of collection; (3) Systems serving <10,000 monitoring one year (24 samples) — bin concentration = arithmetic mean of all samples; (4) Part-year plants with <12 months/year monitoring — bin concentration = highest arithmetic mean in any year of monitoring. If monthly sampling frequency varies, first calculate monthly averages and use those in the applicable calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monthly averaging required when frequency varies. Use the computed bin concentration with the bin threshold table to determine bin classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bin classification thresholds and reporting (§141.710(c)-(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Bin table maps Cryptosporidium bin concentration to bins: <0.075 oocyst/L = Bin 1; 0.075 ≤ conc <1.0 = Bin 2; 1.0 ≤ conc <3.0 = Bin 3; ≥3.0 = Bin 4. Filtered systems must report initial and second-round bin classifications to the State for approval no later than 6 months after required completion of monitoring. Bin classification reports must include a summary of monitoring data and calculation procedures. Failure to comply with reporting conditions is a treatment technique violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting deadlines are strict and failure to report is itself a violation; include data and calculation transparency in submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtered system additional Cryptosporidium treatment by bin and filtration type (§141.711(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Filtered systems must provide additional Cryptosporidium treatment specified by their bin classification and filtration technology. For example, for conventional filtration Bin 2 requires 1-log, Bin 3 requires 2-log, Bin 4 requires 2.5-log; direct filtration and other filtration types have their own log requirements. State may determine equivalence so total removal/inactivation meets specified log targets (e.g., total ≥4.0-log for some determinations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treatment levels vary by filtration technology and bin. State determinations can set equivalence to ensure total log removal/inactivation targets are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of microbial toolbox and minimum crediting for Bin 3/4 (§141.711(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Filtered systems must use one or more treatment and management options listed in § 141.715 (the microbial toolbox) to comply with additional Cryptosporidium treatment. Systems in Bin 3 and Bin 4 must achieve at least 1-log of the additional treatment required using one or a combination of specified options (bag filters, bank filtration, cartridge filters, chlorine dioxide, membranes, ozone, or UV per §§ 141.716–141.720).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At least 1-log must come from microbial toolbox options for higher bins; remaining required treatment must come from other compliant technologies/processes to meet total log requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to achieve treatment credit is a treatment technique violation (§141.711(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure by a system in any month to achieve treatment credit by meeting criteria in §§ 141.716 through 141.720 for microbial toolbox options that is at least equal to the level of treatment required in paragraph (a) of this section is a violation of the treatment technique requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monthly operational compliance is required for credited options; documentation of meeting criteria is necessary to avoid violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: State action when watershed changes post-monitoring (§141.711(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the State determines during a sanitary survey or equivalent assessment that significant changes occurred in the watershed after monitoring was completed that could increase Cryptosporidium contamination, the system must take actions specified by the State, which may include additional source water monitoring and/or implementing microbial toolbox options listed in § 141.715.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State has authority to require responsive monitoring or treatment changes when watershed conditions change, even after initial classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfiltered systems: mean Cryptosporidium level calculation and reporting (§141.712(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Following initial monitoring, unfiltered systems must calculate the arithmetic mean of all Cryptosporidium sample concentrations and report this value to the State for approval no later than 6 months after completion of initial monitoring. After the second round, recalculate and report similarly. If monthly sampling frequency varies, calculate monthly averages first and use those in mean calculations. Reports must include a summary of monitoring data. Failure to comply is a treatment technique violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting deadlines and inclusion of data summaries are required. Monthly averaging used to normalize varying sampling frequencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfiltered systems: Cryptosporidium inactivation requirements (§141.712(b)-(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Unfiltered systems must provide: (1) at least 2-log Cryptosporidium inactivation if mean ≤ 0.01 oocysts/L; (2) at least 3-log inactivation if mean > 0.01 oocysts/L. Unfiltered systems must use chlorine dioxide, ozone, or UV as described in § 141.720 to meet these inactivation requirements. Failure to achieve required inactivation (multiple days for chemical oxidants or failure to meet UV criteria) is a treatment technique violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technology-specific failure modes are enumerated: chemical oxidant users failing more than one day in month are in violation; UV users must meet § 141.720(d)(3)(ii) criteria. Systems must implement and operate approved inactivation technologies to meet logs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of two disinfectants requirement for unfiltered systems (§141.712(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Unfiltered systems must meet combined Cryptosporidium inactivation requirements and Giardia/virus inactivation requirements using a minimum of two disinfectants, and each of the two disinfectants must separately achieve the total inactivation required for either Cryptosporidium, Giardia lamblia, or viruses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redundancy requirement: two disinfectants are required and each must be capable of independently achieving total inactivation for at least one target organism group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule for compliance with Cryptosporidium treatment requirements (§141.713)
rubrics_metrics.description: Following initial bin classification (filtered) or initial mean determination (unfiltered), systems must provide the level of Cryptosporidium treatment required according to the schedule in paragraph (c) of this section (Compliance Dates Table).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance is time-bound; specific compliance dates are provided in the compliance dates table (not included in this chunk). Systems must follow the schedule to avoid treatment technique violations.
